note: Raw output of the competitor-scan workflow run on 2026-10-25 (5 searchers). Feature keys F1-F10 are defined in docs/research/02-competitor-scan.md.

payment-proof.summary:
Short answer: the payment-proof part of Kutip + Bukti already exists, but in separate pieces. None of the products checked combines all of F1-F10 for Malaysian micro B2B sellers.

(1) Closest overall match: Peakflo (Singapore). Its AI WhatsApp Agent sends due, overdue and escalation reminders and claims 40+ languages. It logs payment promises against invoices and collects dispute and short-payment reasons in chat. Customers can upload payment proof in WhatsApp or the portal. It also does 3-way matching of remittance to invoice to bank statement, and has credit freezes. That covers parts of F1, F2, F5, F6, F7 and F8. Pricing is custom-quoted and the SME packages are Singapore grant packages. Malaysia availability is not stated, and no cash-gap ranking (F3) or tiered reminder approval (F4) appeared on the pages checked.

(2) Thai slip verification is mature and cheap. EasySlip costs from 99 THB for 250 checks and reads slip QR or image. It returns amount, receiver, date and reference, detects duplicate slips, and has a LINE group bot. BigSeller's Slip2GO checks the slip against the order amount and returns Partially Paid, Paid or Overpaid. SlipOK (free tier per a third-party repo only) and RDCW are similar. All of these work only with Thai bank slips, which carry a bank-verifiable mini-QR. No Malaysian DuitNow receipt verifier or fake-receipt checker was found, and the one search on this found only bank terms pages.

(3) Enterprise cash-application tools fully cover allocation, short-pays and deductions (F7): HighRadius, Growfin and Versapay. Growfin also logs promise-to-pay (F8). All three are mid-market or enterprise, quote-priced, show no WhatsApp channel, and Malaysia availability is unclear.

(4) Bookkeeping tools that take documents over WhatsApp handle the supplier (AP) side, not customer collections. Dext takes receipts over WhatsApp at USD 25.21/month. Receiptor AI is on Xero's Malaysia app store and matches receipts to existing Xero records before creating new ones.

(5) Lejar.ai is a Malaysian AI ledger. Its paid plans cost RM39, RM89 and RM169 a month, and there is a free plan. It has DuitNow QR on invoices, an AI inbox for receipts, and PDF/CSV bank reconciliation. No reminders, WhatsApp collections or payment-to-invoice matching were seen.

Gaps not found in any product checked:
- F3 cash-gap ranking against payroll, rent and supplier bills
- F4 clerk-versus-owner reminder approval
- F6 parsing of mixed Manglish, BM and Chinese payment replies
- A Malaysian rule that never marks PAID from a slip alone

Absence on these pages is not proof the features do not exist.

Search limits: the shared web-search budget ran out after 10 searches. Indonesian and Philippine verifiers (other than Moota), Malaysian fake-receipt checkers, WhatsApp-native bookkeeping bots, Billtrust, Esker and Bill.com cash application were not fully checked. The Billtrust and Esker pages returned 404, and SlipOK's and G2's sites returned 403. Hubdoc was checked and showed no WhatsApp capture or AR, so it is not in the list.

adversarial.summary:
Verdict: I found no product that does Kutip + Bukti end to end for Malaysian micro B2B sellers. Every feature except F3 does exist in some product, but spread across tools and price bands that miss the target user.

Closest overall is Peakflo (Singapore, sells in SEA). It offers virtual-account collection in Malaysia. It covers:
- yes: F1 (AR tracking), F5 (credit-limit thresholds flag credit freezes), F8 (promise-to-pay logged from WhatsApp free text and used as a reminder trigger), F9 (custom roles and an immutable audit trail).
- partly: F2 (automated WhatsApp reminders with templates; the AI agent claims 40+ languages, but BM and Chinese are not named), F6 (the agent collects promises and short-payment reasons, and customers can upload proof of payment, but reading the image is not claimed), F7 (bank sync plus 3-way matching of remittance, invoice and bank statement; partial matching).
- missing: F3 (no cash forecasting), F4 (no clerk-vs-owner approval on reminders) and F10 (custom pricing; Singapore grant packages start at "up to 1,000 invoices/month").

Next closest:
- Paidnice (NZ; Xero, QBO and Stripe; from USD 69/mo): WhatsApp reminders with pay links, an AI that reads replies and logs promised dates, a person approves every draft, credit stop as an escalation option, and a week-by-week expected-inflow view. No bank-match or slip evidence. Malaysia availability unclear.
- Seenn "Shira" (Israel): a WhatsApp/email/phone AI agent for SMBs on net 30/60/90. It answers replies, books promises and matches payments to invoices. Custom pricing; no Malaysia evidence.
- Enterprise tools (Tesorio, Kolleno): strong on promise extraction, cash application and forecast-led collections, but email-centric and far above micro pricing.
- Malaysian incumbents (Bukku, Mishu) and Whautomate (SG/MY): WhatsApp invoice sending at best. Bukku's auto reminders are email-only, from the RM65 Grow plan. Whautomate shows WhatsApp payment reminders on a tool page; Sales plans start at S$199/mo.
- Regional pieces: BukuWarung (Indonesia, WhatsApp "Tagih" with pay link for micro merchants) and EasySlip (Thailand, slip verification via QR on LINE, from 99 baht/month).

Gaps no product covered in what I could see:
- F3: none of the pages reviewed ranks overdue invoices by how much each closes a forecast shortfall against named outflows (payroll, rent, supplier bills). Tesorio "flags risk and gaps against your targets" from inflows only. Float forecasts outflows but does no collections.
- F4: no clerk-gentle / owner-firm tiered approval anywhere; only Paidnice's approve-everything.
- F6: no evidence of anything parsing mixed Manglish/BM/Chinese replies, or reading payment-slip screenshots, into amount, reference and date.
- F7: no evidence of a check that stops PAID being set from a slip without a bank line.
- F10: no product with WhatsApp plus AI collections priced below RM65/month.

Also seen: an ADA case study of a bespoke WhatsApp collections journey for one Malaysian leasing company (enterprise, not an SME product). CredFlow (India) is listed by third parties as sending WhatsApp reminders; its own site returned 503 and could not be checked.

Limits of this research: the session's web-search budget ran out after 6 searches (the target was 10+). Product Hunt, YC batches, e27, Vulcan Post, Tech in Asia and hackathon winners were not searched, and only one Chinese and one Malay query ran. Everything else comes from about 30 direct fetches of known vendor pages. Statements that a feature is missing are therefore weaker than statements that it exists. A follow-up search pass on those sources is recommended before claiming novelty.

global-ar.summary:
Verdict from the global AR / collections angle: I found no single product that does all of Kutip + Bukti. Two products overlap heavily, though, and the basic layer (F1+F2: tracking invoices and sending WhatsApp reminders) already exists. Do not pitch that layer as new.

Closest overlaps:
(1) PAIDNICE. It is on the Xero App Store Malaysia listing and also works with QuickBooks. Its features page says "Payment reminders on WhatsApp, with a link to pay". Per the Xero listing and its homepage, its AI reads replies, logs promises and drafts the next step for you to approve. Promises are recorded and reminders are held until the promised date. It also offers a "credit stop" escalation, approval of each action, and a weekly cash forecast. It starts at USD 69/month (Essentials, 2 users), which is far above RM65.
(2) PEAKFLO, described in press as a Singaporean fintech. It sends WhatsApp, SMS, LINE and Zalo reminders from templates. Its AI WhatsApp Agent claims 40+ languages, captures promise-to-pay and collects short-payment reasons in chat. It flags credit freezes by limit and runs cash application with partial matching and WHT/discount rules. Pricing is custom and it targets scale-ups to enterprises; Malaysia is not mentioned.

Mid-market and enterprise tools: Upflow, Tesorio and Kolleno now ship AI agents that read replies for promise-to-pay, disputes and remittances. They work over email only; none mention WhatsApp. They start at about USD 545/user/month (Kolleno) or on-request pricing aimed at GBP 10M+ revenue (Upflow).

Accounting tools:
- Xero's built-in reminders are email-only. Xero staff said on 17 June 2026 that WhatsApp sending is not planned.
- Zoho Books can send payment notifications over WhatsApp from templates (April 2024 release). It also pauses reminders when someone enters an expected payment date by hand.
- Third-party WhatsApp layers such as Saysimple already push overdue reminders from Xero and Zoho Books.

Cash-flow tools: Float, Agicap and the forecasting in Chaser and Tesorio show liquidity gaps. None of them ranks overdue invoices by how much each closes a specific upcoming shortfall.

Gaps not seen in any product checked:
- F3: ranking overdue invoices against named outflows ("short RM2,000 for payroll on 31 Oct, chase these 3 first").
- F6: reading payment-slip screenshots. Peakflo only says customers can send proof of payment in WhatsApp.
- F7: checking a slip against the bank-statement line before marking an invoice paid, for micro firms.
- F4: clerk-gentle / owner-firm approval tiers. Paidnice's approval is per action, not by tone tier.
- F2/F6: explicit support for Manglish / BM / Chinese free text.
- F10: pricing under RM65. Only Zoho Books (USD 12/month Standard) and Xero promo plans are near that, and both lack the AI features.

The defensible part is the combination of F3, F6/F7 and micro-firm pricing, not reminders or promise tracking.

Caveats:
- The web search budget ran out after 11 searches. Everything after that was checked by fetching vendor pages directly.
- Pages for Gaviti, Satago, InvoiceSherpa, Fathom, Pulse, Fluidly, FreshBooks and Wave were not checked in depth.
- CredFlow (India, WhatsApp reminders for SMEs) could not be verified because its site returned 503 or an empty page.
- Zoho Malaysia pages returned 404, so MYR pricing was not verified.
- This angle did not cover Malaysian local tools (Bukku, ChatDaddy, etc.).

malaysia-stack.summary:
Short answer: none of the Malaysian tools I checked does all of Kutip + Bukti. But several of its pieces already exist, so the idea is only new on its harder features. The 'Malaysia stack' I checked covers local accounting apps, payment gateways and WhatsApp tools.

What already exists (do not pitch these as new):
- Invoice tracking with automatic reminders (F1): Bukku Grow at RM65, Xero, Zoho Books (Free plan), HitPay (email, no monthly fee) and Biztory.
- WhatsApp sending (F2): Bukku, SQL Account, AutoCount and Biztory send invoices or statements over WhatsApp, as a one-click manual share. SQL Account's eInvoice/Adaptis add-on 'sends payment reminders via email, SMS, WhatsApp'. A 2026 RHB/Xero fact sheet says Xero can send 'invoices or payment reminders directly through WhatsApp'.
- Credit hold (F5): SQL Account already blocks new delivery orders and invoices for overdue customers. AutoCount 2.0 asks for approval when a document exceeds the credit limit.
- Bank reconciliation and allocation (F7, partly): auto bank recon in SQL Account (20+ Malaysian banks, AI matching), AutoCount (Maybank/UOB), Bukku SmartRecon (PDF statements) and Xero. SQL Account can 'knock off all invoices using FIFO, in 1 click'.
- Roles and audit trail (F9): Bukku Prime and AutoCount Cloud.
- Cash flow forecasting (F3, generic only): Xero (30/60/180 days by plan) and Zoho Books Premium.

What I found in none of the products checked:
- F3 as specified: ranking overdue invoices by how much each one closes the next known shortfall ('short RM2,000 for payroll on 31 Oct, chase these 3').
- F4: approval tiers by reminder tone. Zoho and AutoCount have approvals only for sales or purchase documents.
- F6: parsing Manglish/BM/Chinese customer replies and payment-slip screenshots. Every AI or OCR feature found reads supplier bills or receipts.
- F7 as specified: never marking an invoice paid from a slip alone, checking the claimed payment against a bank line, and flagging short-payments or deductions. HitPay and Curlec auto-mark invoices paid only when the money comes through their own rail, not for direct bank transfers.
- F8: promise-to-pay tracking from free-text replies that pauses reminders.
- WhatsApp tools (SleekFlow RM399/month, WATI RM299/month) supply only the messaging channel, with no receivables logic, at roughly 5x Bukku's price.

What this means: the gap is real but narrow. It is the reply/slip-to-bank verification loop (F6, F7 strict, F8) plus cash-gap-driven prioritisation (F3) and tone approval (F4). The likely pitch is a layer on top of the accounting apps SMEs already use, not a replacement for invoicing or reminders.

Limits of this check:
1. I ran 11 web searches before the shared session search budget ran out. Everything after that came from fetching vendor pages directly.
2. Not checked: QuickBooks Malaysia, QNE, Deskera, iPay88, senangPay, toyyibPay, Revenue Monster, Stripe Malaysia, Interakt, and DuitNow Request (the PayNet page returned 403).
3. Billplz's homepage (free Basic plan, DuitNow supported) does not mention reminders or reconciliation.
4. Financio (RM50/month Essentials) lists bank reconciliation and 'A.I. Scan' but no reminders or WhatsApp.
5. respond.io starts at USD 79/month (billed yearly), with WhatsApp fees extra.
6. Zoho Books' availability and pricing in Malaysia are unverified: every Malaysia-specific Zoho URL I tried returned 404.
7. Bukku's help centre needs a login, so its features come only from the public features and pricing pages.
8. 'no' means not found on the public pages fetched. It does not mean the vendor confirmed the feature is absent.
9. Global receivables-collection tools (e.g. Chaser, Paidnice) showed up in search results but were outside this angle and were not checked. They should be checked separately before the team claims novelty.

emerging-markets-micro.summary:
I found nothing in this angle that matches Kutip + Bukti as a whole. The closest analogues only cover F1/F2-lite: a credit ledger plus a one-tap or automatic WhatsApp/SMS reminder with a payment link, usually free.

Evidence limits: about 17 searches ran, plus direct fetches of product pages. The shared session search budget ran out twice. Philippines, Vietnam, Nigeria and Brazil were only partly covered. Khatabook's own site and the Google Play listings would not render, so those rows rest on search snippets and third-party pages.

Malaysia availability:
- The big emerging-market ledgers do not operate in Malaysia. Khatabook, OkCredit, Vyapar, myBillBook and CredFlow are India-focused (UPI, GST); Vyapar adds the UAE. BukuWarung, Paper.id and CrediBook are Indonesia-only.
- BukuKas/Lummo entered voluntary liquidation (DealStreetAsia, 2 Sep 2023).
- Kippa (Nigeria) advertised automated debt reminders in 2022 press coverage, but kippa.africa did not resolve during this check, so its current status is unclear.
- Malaysian 'buku hutang' apps are tiny one-developer apps: BakiMate (one-tap WhatsApp reminder; Urdu/English/Malay; free with Pro at about US$1.99/month), Hutang: Buku Hutang (RM1.90, friends and family, no WhatsApp), Buku 555 (2018, individuals) and Bayar Hutang. Bayar Hutang's older Play listing offered casual/polite/firm reminder tones and its newer one mentions attaching payment proof; its country is unclear. None target B2B sellers on 30-90 day terms.
- WebWMS2U is a Malaysian WhatsApp platform (from RM49/month) that can schedule payment reminders from CSV/Excel. It is generic messaging infrastructure with no ledger and no payment matching.

Gaps (no evidence in any product checked):
- F3: cash-gap prioritisation against payroll/rent. CredFlow shows 'projected cash flows' only.
- F4: tiered clerk/owner approval.
- F6: AI parsing of Manglish/BM/Chinese replies or slip screenshots.
- F8: promise-to-pay tracking that pauses reminders.
- F7, verifying against the bank statement before marking PAID: no product does this. CredFlow lists 'Bank Reconciliation' and Paper.id names AI 'rekonsiliasi', both without detail.
- F2 language mix: no product found sends BM/English/Chinese templates. Vyapar claims multi-language editable templates (Indian languages); OkCredit runs in 11 Indian languages.

Design point for the team: India and Indonesia largely avoid slip-reading. Reminders carry UPI or payment links, and payments are auto-recorded against the customer (OkCredit, BukuWarung, Paper.id). The Malaysian equivalent would be DuitNow/FPX payment links. Kutip + Bukti's F6/F7 value rests on Malaysian B2B buyers paying by bank transfer and sending slips, not through links. Validate that with real sellers.

Other markets: Lista PH sends free SMS/Viber/Messenger reminders (no WhatsApp). Suki PH has WhatsApp reminders for ₱299 one-time. Sổ Bán Hàng (Vietnam) advertises automatic debt reminders without naming the channel. Fiado Zap (Brazil) has automated fiado reminders; its channel is unstated. Fidexa (Brazil) reportedly uses AI on WhatsApp to collect small retail debts via Pix. That is a consumer-retail analogue to F6, seen only in a search snippet and not verified.

Verdict for this angle: the 'ledger + WhatsApp reminder' core is commoditised and free in emerging markets. The F3 + F4 + F6 + F7 + F8 combination for Malaysian B2B credit sellers was not found.
